meta.title: Qbasis.One | An Oasis In Your Quantum Computing Desert
meta.description: Start your quantum computing journey with Qbasis.One.

announce.text: The QASIS platform preview is in preparation

hero.sub: Qbasis.One builds a development environment for quantum software. Define the problem with a matrix and a function; the DSL synthesizes the circuit, and the platform runs it and returns the results.

platform.title: Author locally. Execute remotely.
platform.body: The Qbasis platform has three parts: the DSL, the execution platform, and the execution backends. The only thing that leaves your machine is a submission.

cards.title: Quantum DSL
cards.body: Circuit synthesis, cost-function building, and optimization run locally. Shipped as a Python SDK.

cards.title: Execution platform
cards.body: Manages submissions, queues, sessions, and stored results. Job status and convergence curves are viewable on the web.

cards.title: Execution backends
cards.body: Runs on our own GPU simulator. Quantum hardware (QPU) access is being prepared behind the same submission format.

features.title: Write only the code that defines the algorithm
features.body: Block encoding, polynomial approximation, phase-factor computation, and reading measurement results are handled by the DSL.

items.title: Say what to solve
items.body: Assembling the same linear system from a general-purpose quantum SDK's gates means getting every listed item correct by hand. If one is wrong, the circuit still runs and only the answer is wrong. With the DSL it is two lines that take the matrix A and the function f.

items.title: Circuits grow linearly as the grid grows
items.body: The DSL picks a block encoding that uses the matrix structure (banded Toeplitz). Each extra grid qubit adds about 820 gates to the DSL circuit, while loading the whole matrix as one unitary multiplies its CX count by about 4.7.

items.title: Variational loops run inside a session
items.body: Each iteration submits the objective and its gradient evaluations as one job. The session records iterations in order to build the convergence curve, and the same curve is shown on the web.

compare.dslNote: You decide: the matrix A, the function f, and the block-encoding kind
compare.sdkLabel: Hand-built with a general-purpose quantum SDK

measured.title: We publish what we measured

tiles.fidelityBody: Agreement Σ√(p·q) between the GPU simulator's 32,768-shot distribution and the numerical target f(A)b. Identical distributions score 1.

measured.quote: We do not claim quantum advantage. We build the toolchain so the code is already there when the hardware is ready.
measured.footnote: Measured in-house in August 2026 on one step of an implicit Black–Scholes FDM (8 grid points) solved with a QSVT regularized inverse. The comparison is the same problem assembled by hand from a general-purpose quantum SDK's gates.

items.title: No quantum-advantage claims
items.body: The example circuits are beyond what today's NISQ hardware runs. What we provide is the code and the pipeline from problem definition to execution.

items.title: Verification ships with results
items.body: Simulator results are checked against the classical solution. Error and post-selection success rate go into the results table as measured.

items.title: Same submission, same result
items.body: Every submission carries a reproducible key. Sending the same submission again returns the earlier result instead of running it twice.

cta.title: When the hardware is ready, the code is already there
cta.body: Preview access and adoption inquiries are handled by email.

items.a: It is not a public service yet. Email us if you would like to join the preview.

items.q: Do I need to know quantum circuits?
items.a: If you can define the problem as a matrix and a function, you can call the synthesis functions. The one argument that picks the block encoding follows from the matrix structure.

items.q: Which backends does it run on?
items.a: Today it runs on our own GPU simulator. Quantum hardware (QPU) access is being prepared behind the same submission format.

items.q: How is it different from a general-purpose quantum SDK?
items.a: General-purpose SDKs assemble circuits gate by gate. The Qbasis DSL takes a problem definition such as a matrix, a function, or an observable, synthesizes the circuit, and carries it through submission and result retrieval.
A quantum DSL, execution middleware, and an adoption service that brings a quantum computing environment into your organization.
